mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 4% in the month preceding the prediction triggers a term premium compression, lowering discount rates and pushing up near-term equity valuations, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the preceding month
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day rolling mean of the same period when FEDFUNDS crosses above 4%, or term premium spread (SP500_MV - 10Y_TMT) does not widen by at least 0.5 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent declines in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over three consecutive months signal deflationary expectations, reducing real discount rates and supporting equity valuations, which predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls for three consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically outperforming the 30-day rolling mean during the three-month CPI decline, or the 10Y real yield does not fall by more than 5 basis points.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden jump in employment growth (PAYEMS) above 200,000 jobs in a month is interpreted as a labor market strengthening, lowering risk premia and increasing investor optimism, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS exceeds 200,000 in a single month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive in 70% of months where PAYEMS > 200,000, or the 10-day volatility does not decline by at least 10% during the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in industrial production (INDPRO) accompanied by a decline in consumer demand proxies (HOUST) indicates a structural shift toward business-driven growth, which lowers growth risk premia and supports equity valuations, predicting positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by ≥ 5% while HOUST falls by ≥ 3% in the same month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns underperform the 30-day rolling mean during such INDPRO/HOUST cross-patterns, or the 5-year realized volatility does not decline by more than 15%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial supply (INDPRO) below 100 for two consecutive months, despite stable or rising employment, suggests supply-side bottlenecks that persist into the near term, raising growth expectations and pushing up equity valuations, which predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO remains below 100 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive during the two-month INDPRO contraction, or the 10-day implied volatility does not rise by at least 2 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment claims (UNRATE) above 5.5% signals weakening labor market conditions, which raises perceived risk and compresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 5.5% in a month
regime_hint: early signs of labor market stress
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative in months where UNRATE > 5.5%, or the 5-day realized volatility does not increase by at least 8%.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of negative real yields (CPIAUCSL deflation minus FEDFUNDS) exceeding 2 basis points for 30 consecutive days is interpreted as a structural yield inversion that amplifies equity demand, predicting positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL - FEDFUNDS < -2 bps for 30 consecutive days
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns underperform the 30-day rolling mean during the 30-day negative real yield streak, or the 10-year real yield does not fall by more than 20 basis points.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of falling retail sales (HOUST) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) indicate deteriorating consumer demand, which raises recession risk and compresses equity valuations, predicting negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls for two consecutive months while UNRATE rises for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative in 80% of such demand weakness episodes, or the 5-day realized volatility does not increase by at least 12%.
